hook: One neonatal antisense dose rescued autism-like behavior and hippocampal damage in mice with a GRIA1 variant.
summary: Mice carrying the autism-linked GRIA1 A636T variant showed autism-like behavior and progressive hippocampal neuron loss from excitotoxicity, because their AMPA receptors never switched to the calcium-impermeable form. A single allele-specific antisense oligonucleotide given at birth prevented the damage. It is a mouse model, and treatment so early may be hard to match in people.
title: Antisense oligonucleotide silencing rescues neurodevelopmental deficits in AMPA receptor gain-of-function mice.
